name: EncodeDecode
caption: Encode / Decode

configuration.description: "encode" converts plain text into the format, "decode" converts the format back into plain text. Case-insensitive. A missing value means decode. Any other value fails the step and gives a publish warning. The editor always writes it.

The coding: base64, base64url (URL alphabet -_ without padding), urlForm (space as +), urlPath (space as %20), xml, html, json (escape/unescape of the content, no surrounding quotes), quotedPrintable (RFC 2045), rfc2047 (MIME header encoded words such as =?utf-8?B?...?=), regex (encode only). Case-insensitive. A missing value means base64. Any other value fails the step and gives a publish warning. The editor always writes it.
The value to encode or decode, usually a SmartField such as "{{GetAttachments_contentBytes}}". Resolved before the step runs. An empty resolved value gives an empty result, not an error.

outputs.name: result
outputs.when: always; the encoded or decoded text ('' for an empty input). Large values (hundreds of KB) are stored completely.

rules.check: configuration.direction, when present, must be "encode" or "decode" (case-insensitive)
rules.message: Encode / Decode step '%1': Direction '%2' is unknown. Use encode or decode.

rules.check: configuration.format, when present, must be one of the format codes (case-insensitive)
rules.message: Encode / Decode step '%1': Format '%2' is unknown. Use base64, base64url, urlForm, urlPath, xml, html, json, quotedPrintable, rfc2047 or regex.

rules.check: format "regex" must not be combined with direction "decode"
rules.message: Encode / Decode step '%1': RegEx escape can only encode. Use the direction Encode.

rules.check: configuration.input must be present and non-empty
rules.message: Encode / Decode step '%1': Enter the input to encode or decode.

rules.check: direction, format and input are required fields in the configuration dialog
rules.message: Please fill in the highlighted fields.

rules.check: An unknown direction or format code, or regex with decode, fails the step before anything is converted
rules.message: Direction '%1' is unknown. Use encode or decode. | Format '%1' is unknown. Use base64, base64url, urlForm, urlPath, xml, html, json, quotedPrintable, rfc2047 or regex. | RegEx escape can only encode. Use the direction Encode.

rules.check: Decode input that is not valid in the format: base64/base64url with invalid characters or length, JSON-escaped text with an unescaped " or an escape other than \" \\ \/ \b \f \n \r \t \uXXXX, a Quoted-Printable '=' not followed by two hex digits or a line break, a broken RFC 2047 B/Q payload
An RFC 2047 encoded word names a character set other than UTF-8, ISO-8859-1, Windows-1252 or US-ASCII
rules.message: The character set %1 is not supported in RFC 2047 encoded words. Supported are UTF-8, ISO-8859-1, Windows-1252 and US-ASCII.

notes: Text is UTF-8 in both directions. Base64 decode returns text: decoding binary content such as a PDF to text loses data - keep binary content as base64 and pass the base64 to steps that accept it.
Base64 and Base64URL decode ignore spaces, tabs and line breaks (MIME wraps base64 at 76 characters).

Quoted-Printable decode always interprets the bytes as UTF-8; ISO-8859-1 content shows wrong umlauts. Encode writes =XX for every non-printable byte and '=', soft line breaks keep lines at 76 characters, line breaks become CRLF.

RFC 2047 decode replaces every encoded word in the text and keeps plain text; whitespace between two adjacent encoded words is removed. Encode returns pure printable ASCII unchanged, otherwise =?utf-8?B?...?= words of at most 75 characters joined by a space.

XML and HTML encode write the five entities & < > " ' (HTML writes ' as '). Decode resolves numeric entities; HTML decode also the named HTML 4 / Latin-1 entities ( , ä, €, –, ...). Unknown entities and a lone & stay unchanged.
The Debug execution log contains a summary line, the input and the result.

Typical use: Microsoft Graph returns an S/MIME signed mail as one attachment smime.p7m (contentType multipart/signed) whose contentBytes hold the whole MIME message. Decode it with base64, cut the parts with a Parser (RegEx) step, decode file names with rfc2047; the PDF part body is already base64.
